title: God doesn’t always remove giants—He trains giant killers.
paragraphs: God doesn’t always remove giants—He trains giant killers.

Some of you have been praying for the battle to disappear, while God has been using the battle to develop what prayer alone could not produce without pressure: courage, discernment, endurance, and faith that knows how to stand when the ground shakes.
“Blessed be the Lord my strength, which teacheth my hands to war, and my fingers to fight.” — Psalm 144:1
But here’s what most people don’t realize…

The giant in front of you may not be proof that God has left you.
It may be proof that God is training you.

David was not made in the spotlight.
He was formed in secret.
A lion. A bear. Isolation. Worship. Obedience.
So when Goliath appeared, the public only saw a moment.
God saw a history of preparation.
And that is where many people miss the story.

The real battle is never just the giant outside of you.
It is the fear within you.
The doubt within you.
The sin that whispers, “You are not enough.”
And on your own, you are not.
That is why the gospel matters here.

You do not become a giant killer by self-belief, hustle, or religious performance.
You become strong when you are surrendered to Jesus Christ.
Sin made us weak.
Pride made us wander.
But grace stepped in.

Jesus did not come merely to improve brave people.
He came to save dead sinners.
He lived the life we could not live, died the death we deserved, and rose again so that through repentance and faith, we could be redeemed, changed, and empowered by God.

So yes, God trains hands for war.
But first, He rescues hearts from sin.

Originally written by Gospel Warrior, this is your reminder that the battle did not come to destroy every child of God.
Sometimes it came to reveal who truly trusts Him.

If this found you, it’s not by accident.
There’s a deeper word here than one post can hold.

And when the next giant stands in front of you, do not ask first, “Why is this here?”
Ask, “What has God been building in me for this moment?”
Because every battle bows eventually before the Lordship of Jesus.
